A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LGKT research, with matching authors, algorithms and benchmarks. All supplied pages and appendices are readable, and relocated text and renumbered figures can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on synthetic MDPs, JumpRiverSwim, FrozenLake and AnyTrading, including benchmark comparisons and threshold ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds evaluations of adaptive thresholds, adaptive switching and uniform-exploration variants in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Appendices E.3–E.4 add state-visit-based threshold increases and a switching-time rule, tc = sqrt(SAT), for the existing LG1-2T hybrid. These are additional tuning procedures; the underlying LG1T/LGKT algorithms and previously implemented UCB fallback remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic MDP settings, JumpRiverSwim state spaces, 4-by-4 FrozenLake and episodic AnyTrading environment. The added studies examine algorithm variants within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The six external RL baselines and two oracle policies are retained. New Figures 10–12 additionally evaluate LG1T-Uniform and LG2T-Uniform against the implemented UCB variants; these theoretical variants were described but not empirically compared in v1.

E3.justification: New supplementary comparisons introduce threshold-growth settings, the sqrt(SAT) switching rule and uniform-versus-UCB exploration controls. The retained benchmark experiments keep their 20,000-interaction budget, environment generation, thresholds and manually specified switching times.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's fixed-threshold sensitivity analysis, v2 adds studies testing automatic threshold selection, automatic switching between lookahead depths, and whether empirical performance depends on replacing theoretical uniform exploration with UCB. The original threshold ablations remain in E.6 as Figures 13–18.

E5.justification: Reported averaging remains 100 repetitions for JumpRiverSwim and FrozenLake and 1,000 for AnyTrading. Shaded curves occur in both versions; v2 adds no seed information, uncertainty definitions, significance tests or changed statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figures 5–12 add substantial results on adaptive tuning and exploration variants. Adaptive switching improves over LG1T on synthetic MDPs but can trail LG2T; uniform exploration shows strong threshold sensitivity and can fall below PMEVI-KLUCRL on JumpRiverSwim. The main reported competitive ratios, 0.75/0.96 and 0.80/0.94, are retained. Figure 9 duplicates Figure 8, leaving its claimed FrozenLake result unsupported.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.4 is broadened from greedy to thresholding policies, with an expanded argument in B.2. New Theorem 3.5 and Appendix B.3 provide a claimed transition-distance suboptimality bound. Appendix F adds a claimed O(sqrt(SAT log(T))) regret bound and proof for the already implemented UCB-based LG1T variant.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims about truncated lookahead, thresholding, regret guarantees, superior finite-horizon rewards and hybrid warm-starting. The new supporting studies do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds arguments for near-optimality under similar action transitions, asymptotic optimality through increasing thresholds, and a favorable regime for fast convergence in Remark 4.7. It also interprets the new exploration controls as showing when UCB improves robustness. The existing threshold tradeoff discussion is relocated from C.2 rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a link to the authors' implementation. Appendices E.3–E.4 and their figures specify threshold increments and the switching-time formula for the new variants. Existing environment-generation and baseline-implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and positioning against prior research remain unchanged. The Pla et al. lookahead reference is updated from a 2025 preprint to its 2026 AISTATS publication, rather than introducing a different work.

P1.justification: v2 moves threshold-selection discussion into Section 4.2, adds appendix subsections and proof material, and makes localized wording and notation edits. Publication and conflict-of-interest text are updated, while the main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 5–12 and substantially reformats retained appendix plots, now Figures 13–18, including legend placement, proportions and axes. Main-text figures are relocated. Some new captions reverse panel descriptions, and Figure 9 repeats Figure 8 under a FrozenLake caption.

improvement.justification: The added tuning studies, exploration controls and code link address practical gaps in v1. However, new Theorem 3.5 permits a zero loss bound for identical transitions even when differently rewarded actions pass the threshold and cause positive loss; Appendix B.3 does not resolve this. Figure 9 also duplicates JumpRiverSwim evidence under a FrozenLake caption. Useful empirical additions coexist with substantive new theoretical and reporting defects, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
